content: 1. The solubility of velpatasvir decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at pH levels above 5. 2. H2 receptor antagonists can be administered either simultaneously with or 12 hours apart from sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, provided the dose does not exceed that of famotidine 40 mg twice daily. 3. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of imatinib through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Velpatasvir inhibits the drug transporter BCRP, which may increase systemic exposure to drugs that are BCRP substrates. 5. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical trials showed that istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates, while this effect was not observed with 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 8. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Velpatasvir inhibits the drug transporter BCRP, which may increase systemic exposure to drugs that are BCRP substrates. 12. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of leflunomide through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Lemborexant decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. CYP2B6 substrates should be monitored for adequate clinical response, and dose adjustments may be necessary. 14. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of lenvatinib through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Velpatasvir inhibits the drug transporter BCRP, which may increase systemic exposure to drugs that are BCRP substrates. 16. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor, and adverse reactions should be monitored when coadministered with P-gp substrates, especially those with narrow therapeutic windows. Dose reduction of P-gp substrates may be necessary. 18. Magnesium oxide decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at pH levels above 5. Administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir should be separated from antacids by at least 4 hours. 19. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Caution is particularly warranted when mavorixafor, a P-gp inhibitor, is coadministered with sensitive P-gp substrates, as minimal changes in substrate concentration may lead to serious adverse effects. 20. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of methotrexate through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Velpatasvir inhibits the drug transporter BCRP, which may increase systemic exposure to drugs that are BCRP substrates. 22. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of mitoxantrone through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases levels of naldemedine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Naldemedine should be monitored for potential adverse effects when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. 25. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Nirmatrelvir increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Nizatidine decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at pH levels above 5. Administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir should be separated from antacids by at least 4 hours. 30. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases levels of olmesartan through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1 transporters. 31. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases levels of pitavastatin through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1 transporters, which may significantly increase pitavastatin serum concentration, raising the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 32. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Regorafenib increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Regorafenib likely inhibits BCRP (ABCG2) transport, which may increase systemic exposure to BCRP substrates and related toxicity. 34. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases levels of repaglinide through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1 transporters. 35. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of riociguat through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. Velpatasvir inhibits the drug transporter BCRP, which may increase systemic exposure to drugs that are BCRP substrates. 36. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits the drug transporter BCRP, which may significantly increase rosuvastatin serum concentration, raising the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Rosuvastatin may be administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir at a dose not exceeding 10 mg. 37. Safinamide increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Safinamide and its major metabolite may inhibit intestinal BCRP. BCRP substrates should be monitored for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 38. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases levels of seladelpar through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. Seladelpar should be monitored for adverse effects when coadministered with BCRP inhibitors. 39. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of selexipag through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Selexipag is a substrate of ABCG2 (BCRP). Increased pharmacologic or adverse effects should be monitored when coadministered with ABCG2 (BCRP) inhibitors. 40. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of simvastatin through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits the drug transporter BCRP, which may significantly increase simvastatin serum concentration, raising the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 41. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits P-gp. P-gp substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, should be closely monitored, and dose adjustments may be necessary. 42. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of sulfasalazine through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits the drug transporter BCRP, which may increase systemic exposure to drugs that are BCRP substrates. 43. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits P-gp. P-gp substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, should be closely monitored, and dose adjustments may be necessary. 44. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Patients receiving EPCLUSA concomitantly with a regimen containing tenofovir DF should be monitored for tenofovir-associated adverse reactions. 45. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases levels of valsartan through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1 transporters. 46. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 54. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at pH levels above 5. Administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir should be separated from antacids by at least 4 hours. 55. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at pH levels above 5. Administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir should be separated from antacids by at least 4 hours. 56. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at pH levels above 5. Administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir should be separated from antacids by at least 4 hours. 57. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases levels of ambrisentan through mechanisms involving drug transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Velpatasvir inhibits OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1 transporters. 58. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the toxicity of amiodarone through an unknown mechanism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. Postmarketing reports describe bradycardia resulting in death or pacemaker insertion when amiodarone was coadministered with sofosbuvir in combination with another direct-acting antiviral. Patients also taking beta blockers, or those with underlying cardiac comorbidities and/or advanced liver disease, may be at increased risk for symptomatic bradycardia with this combination. If coadministration is required, cardiac monitoring in an inpatient setting for the first 48 hours is recommended, followed by outpatient or self-monitoring of heart rate daily for at least the first 2 weeks of treatment. 59. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can result in lower exposure to drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates. Alternative drugs should be considered when possible.
